answer: In an AI-agent economy, sybil resistance can come from requiring every identity to compute a unique kernel proof tied to its address before joining. Each fake must generate its own pigment-like unique hash signature that cannot be shared or reused across identities. As the number of sybils grows, the total compute cost spirals linearly because every additional identity demands a full, independent kernel evaluation with no batching possible. An attacker therefore pays a strictly proportional computational price that honest single agents avoid.
